name: dns-cn-fallback-embedded-nul-evades-constraint-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees dNSName is example.com. The leaf has no SAN, only a subject DN whose CN bytes spell 'example.com', then 00, then 'evil.com'. GnuTLS (and some other libraries) fall back to consulting the CN as a hostname for dNSName constraint matching when the cert lacks a DNS SAN. A length-correct comparison sees the full CN value 'example.com\x00evil.com' which is not equal to example.com and is not a subdomain of it, so the leaf must be rejected. A C-string comparison sees 'example.com' (truncated at the NUL) and incorrectly accepts.
references: DEFCON 17 (Marlinspike) 'Null Prefix Attacks Against SSL/TLS Certificates'
notes: Mirror of dn-cn-embedded-nul-evades-constraint-invalid, but the constraint is a dNSName constraint (not a directoryName) so the validator's CN-as-hostname fallback path is what's exercised — not the DN-vs-DN comparator. GnuTLS lib/x509/name_constraints.c lines ~1860-1895 walks all CN attributes via gnutls_x509_crt_get_dn_by_oid and feeds them into the DNSNAME constraint check; this is the path most likely to be C-string-truncated.
Constructed via subject_der_ascii2der so the NUL byte inside the CN UTF8String is unambiguous in the source.

certs.subject: C=US,O=NC Tests,CN=DNS CN NUL Leaf
certs.subject_der_ascii2der: SEQUENCE { SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.6 } PrintableString { "US" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.10 } UTF8String { "NC Tests" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.3 } UTF8String { `6578616d706c652e636f6d006576696c2e636f6d` } } } }
